newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent weaker.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent weaker.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.20 cent weaker Tuesday, based on market orders at 1020 EDT, dealers said.
USDA said Monday that 65 percent of the crop had been planted, compared with 64 percent last year and 65 percent in a five-year average.

Traders said the USDA report, coupled with a weak technical close on Monday, could pressure prices early. The market is not likely to react to the spec/hedge report, which showed the speculators to be holding a net 19.4 percent short position, barely changed from last week.
Monday, July ended down 0.66 cent at 72.38 cents a lb after trading from 73.30 to 72.30 cents. New-crop December finished 0.43 cent lower at 74.80 cents.
Volume was estimated at a thin 6,000 lots.
Nearby resistance was seen at 73.50 cents followed by 74.10 cents, where buy stops are expected to be resting, for July cotton, according to traders.
